title: Kenyan Wedding Beef Pilau
community: Enjoyed across all Kenyan communities at weddings
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Wedding Beef Pilau — the grandest expression of Kenyan pilau. Made for 20+ guests at weddings, the rice is richly spiced, the beef is the finest cut, and the preparation is a community effort. The meal that marks the most important day in a Kenyan family's life.
longDesc: Wedding pilau is the ultimate expression of the pilau tradition — made on a scale that requires multiple cooks, enormous sufurias, and a full day of preparation. The wedding pilau cook (often a renowned local cook hired specifically for the occasion) is one of the most important wedding vendors in Kenya. This recipe scales to 20 portions — a small wedding batch.
ingredients: 10 cups basmati rice — washed and soaked
steps: Toast all spices in a dry pan until deeply fragrant. Grind half, keep half whole.
In the large sufuria, heat oil until very hot. Brown beef in large batches.
Cook onions until deeply golden — 15 minutes for this quantity.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, and tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes until very thick.
Return all beef. Add stock. Simmer covered for 45—50 minutes.
Drain soaked rice. Add to pot. Stir gently.
Bring to a boil, reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly with lid and a cloth.
Rest 15 minutes. Fold gently. Garnish generously with coriander.
chefTips: For wedding scale, prepare the spice blend and cook the beef the day before — assemble with rice on the day.
The cloth under the lid absorbs excess steam and prevents the rice from becoming too wet — the wedding cook's secret.
Taste and adjust salt after the beef step and again after the rice is cooked.
commonMistakes: Under-seasoning at scale — the spice proportions need to be maintained at larger quantities.
Insufficient resting — wedding pilau must rest at least 15 minutes.
cookingScience: At wedding scale, heat distribution becomes more challenging — the sufuria's base receives much more heat than the sides. The cloth under the lid and thorough resting help equalise temperature and moisture distribution throughout the large volume of rice.
sustainabilityTips: Wedding pilau creates a powerful argument for local beef procurement — contact local cattle farmers to source wedding quantities sustainably.
reheating: Reheat in large covered pot over low heat.
culturalNote: Wedding pilau is the culinary centrepiece of the most important day in a Kenyan family's life. The skill of the pilau cook is a point of family pride — and the taste and quality of the wedding pilau is discussed in the community for months afterwards.
